blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (GET /invoices/:id returns any organization's invoice) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Insecure direct object reference (CWE-639 / CWE-862). Any signed-in user of organization 7 who sends `GET /invoices/42` receives invoice 42 even when it belongs to another organization: the query filters on `id` only, and ids are sequential numbers easy to enumerate. Scope the query to the caller's organization, as the list endpoint does — `WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2` with `[id, currentUser(req).orgId]` — and keep answering 404 when no row matches, so the existence of other organizations' invoices is not revealed. Add a test where the invoice belongs to another organization and the answer is 404.
findings.title: GET /invoices/:id returns any organization's invoice

findings.recommendation: Information exposure through an error message (CWE-209). An unauthenticated client that sends a malformed JSON body (`Content-Type: application/json`, body `{`) to any route makes `express.json()` raise a parse error, which reaches this handler and is answered with its full stack trace — server file paths, dependency versions — and, for errors raised further in, database or driver messages. Log the error server-side only and answer a generic body such as `{ "error": "internal error" }`; respect `err.status` for client errors such as the 400 of a bad JSON body instead of turning them into 500.
findings.title: Error handler returns the error message and stack trace to any client

findings.recommendation: The id is checked to be an integer but not bounded: `GET /invoices/1e19` passes `Number.isInteger` and is sent to PostgreSQL, which rejects it as out of range for an integer or bigint column. The handler is `async` and Express 4.19.2 does not forward a rejected promise to the error handler, so the rejection is unhandled — with Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` any signed-in user can crash the process with one request. Validate the id against an allow-list at the boundary (`/^\d{1,9}$/` or a positive safe integer within the column's range), and wrap the async handlers so a rejection reaches `next(err)`. Confidence is low: the column type and the Node runtime and its process supervision were not visible.
findings.title: Unbounded numeric id reaches the database and its rejection escapes Express
